quest.title: The Power of Research
quest.description: You stumble upon someone calling for help in a thunderstorm, and he seems to definitely need some...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.text: I can't imagine how you two warriors managed to make it through the thunderstorm, but... that's not the point right now. I need your help!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, there's no way we'd stand by while someone needs help. What do you need us to do?
Please, help me get the <color=#00E1FFFF>Airspace Data Collector</color> up in the air!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Airspace Data Collector...? You mean that big round machine?
That's right! All you need to do is <color=#00E1FFFF>align the strong kuuvahki side of each assembly module with the collector, and push them into place</color>.
Then the collector — ah, I mean that big round machine — will float up into the air. That means everything's working!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Alright, seeing how desperate you are... Let's help him out, {NICKNAME}.
Thank you so much! I really appreciate it!
Please, don't strike me... I still have work to do!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Good news! I've made a breakthrough!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I'm 99.5% sure that the Fanngel Effect didn't affect either of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's great, though Paimon wasn't really concerned about that... But if it wasn't because of the Fanngel Effect, then why did the collector get struck last time?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Because the lightning protection device inside the collector was never tested for repeated use in such a high kuuvahki environment. The materials eventually gave out from fatigue.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: The fix was actually pretty simple. I tested a bunch of materials with different parameters based on this area's kuuvahki concentration, and found something way more durable. Look—

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: This is the <color=#00E1FFFF>Nod-Krai Airspace Data Collector 2.0</color> — I stayed up all night to finish it. With one final high-altitude test, we'll be able to determine the experiment's results!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is the Collector 2.0 so much smaller than the previous one?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Advanced models are usually more compact.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, Paimon gets it now! So, Paimon really is more advanced than {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Hehe... While that's usually true, the reason the 2.0 model shrank so much this time was actually due to the limits of the materials used. I had to cut a lot of non-essential features—

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: For example, the entire structure for lifting it into the air...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? If it can't get up in the air, how is it supposed to collect data from high altitudes?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Uhm... Well... Ah — It's all because... You see... Many of the greatest leaps in human knowledge come when the researchers themselves step in. Even if it means becoming the subject of their own experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: They say Heinry's team drank tens of thousands of bottles of Fonta to perfect the flavor we have today. So... You get what I'm saying, right?

choices.text: Not really.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Staring at us won't make us understand, you know.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: *sigh* You are way too smart not to get this. But fine, if you insist...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: #How about this — I'll just redesign the Fannta bottle to be shaped like you two... or we don't even have to call it Fannta anymore. It could be Paita, Monta, or {NICKNAME}-ta.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Please, for the sake of scientific progress, take the Collector 2.0 with you into the skies!

choices.text: Since it's for scientific progress, I'll do it.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Oh, so you already have a glider! That's amazing! Then we can check that off the list.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Alright, let me explain the latest changes! Just yesterday, it occurred to me... since the thunderstorms here are bursting with kuuvahki...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Instead of avoiding it, why not harness it? In other words, we can actively attract the lightning! This relay device was built for exactly that purpose.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Attract the lightning!? But that sounds dangerous!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: You'll be fine. Most of the kuuvahki in the thunderstorm will be converted into an upward force field. The remaining energy will be captured by the Collector 2.0 to power the enhanced lightning protection device.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Trust me, your chances of getting struck are no higher than 0.0067%.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So there's still a chance Paimon might get struck...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: S—Statistically speaking, there's a negligible risk. I mean, no proper scientist would ever claim something is 100% certain...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: This will be the final experiment. <color=#00E1FFFF>Channel the lightning to the lightning rod over there, then launch up and collect the data.</color> The lightning protection device in the Collector 2.0 will keep you safe.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: I'll let you know as soon as we've got enough data. And I'll do everything I can to keep you safe. So, ready to go?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: For the sake of science.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: That's the spirit — for the sake of science!

choices.text: Since it's for scientific progress... How about Paimon does it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? We're both part of this co-branding, aren't we? Then why is Paimon the only one being sent off...?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: I'm not sure that'll do... Even in the name of scientific progress, we can't run experiments on someone so small! I was just thinking of making you a glider or something...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I've got one already. I was only joking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You gave Paimon a scare... Don't joke around like that! But don't worry, Paimon will be going with you, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: You want to conduct the experiment yourself?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Huh!? Not me! It's enough of a miracle that the Fanngel Effect hasn't affected you two. If I were the one to try it, it'd be a total disaster...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Not that I'd mind trying. Sooner or later, the curse will devour me anyway. But the research on kuuvahki is too important to be left unfinished...

talks.objective: Push each assembly module to the correct orientation and position

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing. Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Oh, right! I just noticed that <color=#00E1FFFF>there's a signal issue in one of the three channels, but it can be fixed by resetting the robot</color>. Now, let me set up the experimental parameters!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, just give me a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll inspect the collector's hardware in the meantime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing. Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Oh, right! I just noticed that <color=#00E1FFFF>there's a signal issue in one of the three channels, but it can be fixed by resetting the robot</color>. Now, let me set up the experimental parameters!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

talks.objective: Push each assembly module to the correct orientation and position

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: The experiment was a success! Just as I thought, kuuvahki has huge potential!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Thank you both. This is the critical data I was missing. Once I've combed through it all, I can finally get started on my thesis.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I hope the research results on kuuvahki will truly achieve what Mr. Raimondo envisioned — freeing people from their reliance on Arkhium. This would be an enormous step forward.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we actually helped with something big. That's awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Indeed, progress marches forward! My thesis should be done in a year or two. And maybe in twenty or thirty more, we'll start to see the real impact of what we did today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: T—Twenty or t—thirty years?! That long?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: That sort of time frame is already a breakneck breakthrough! Scientific research takes time, you know. It's all about patience and precision. We can't rush it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Alright, fine... Paimon really thought we'd get to try a bottle of Fann-{NICKNAME}-Paimon-ta any day now...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I'll be sure to suggest that to Heinry and the team! Oh, and here, take the Nod-Krai Airspace Data Collector 2.0 as thanks from me.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I've removed the data collection module, since it's classified tech from the Institute. I hope you understand.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: It no longer has any data collection functionality, but the lightning protection still works. Hopefully, it'll come in handy on your adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Just a heads-up! It only works on thunderstorms that carry kuuvahki. It won't be effective against regular lightning, so once you're outside Nod-Krai, it probably won't be of much use...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! That means we don't have to worry about getting struck by lightning while we're out exploring!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Science really can defeat a curse!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Haha, well said! And finally, thank you both again for your contribution to science. Once I've sorted through the raw data, it's time for me to head back to the Institute and start writing my thesis.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: We'll need higher-altitude data this time, so <color=#00E1FFFF>we'll need to stack three assembly modules for each channel</color>. However, you only need to manually adjust the modules for two of the channels. Leave the rest to me.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: We'll need higher-altitude data this time, so <color=#00E1FFFF>we'll need to stack three assembly modules for each channel</color>. However, you only need to manually adjust the modules for two of the channels. Leave the rest to me.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Fanngel finishes setting the parameters for the experiment.

talks.objective: Push each assembly module to the designated position

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, just give me a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll inspect the collector's hardware in the meantime.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fanngel! Th—There was an accident... The collector got hit by lightning...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Yes, I saw it too. The Fanngel Effect... It's intensified. Even with the lightning protection device and your help, we can't hold it back...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Well, things might not be that bad. Don't give up just yet...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The only way to break the curse is by advancing science.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly. According to your theory, the only one who can defeat the Fanngel Effect now is you, Fanngel!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Oh! You're right. If I fail, this curse won't just destroy me. It will destroy everything I hold dear.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: If, in the end, even the Fontaine Research Institute is... is... I would never forgive myself.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: We're at a critical stage of the experiment. Based on my initial analysis, kuuvahki does indeed seem safer than Arkhium.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: But for real-world applications, that conductive phenomenon we just observed must never be allowed to happen. I have to identify the cause.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: The collector's crashed... It's certainly unfortunate, but what really matters is the data inside. Could I ask you to retrieve it for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, leave it to us.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Please be careful! I'll check here to see if the issue was caused by the equipment itself.

talks.objective: Find the crashed collector and recover the experiment data
Bring the experiment data to Fanngel

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I was starting to worry the Fanngel Effect might've gotten to you, too... So, how did it go? Did you get the data?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We got it, but the collector was already...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I suspected as much... The designs never accounted for the impact from a fall. *sigh* That was my oversight.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I've found a few leads on my end as well, but it's too early to draw any conclusions. I'll need to analyze them together with the data you recovered.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Give me some time to dig into it. Could you come by again tomorrow?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've got the data! So that means we're done here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but we still need data from higher altitudes... That's how scientific research works. It's all about patience and precision. We can't rush it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, but... you didn't get struck by lightning when you went to set the parameters just now, did you? Maybe that curse of yours isn't as bad as you think! So for this next experiment...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: No, no! It has to be the two of you conducting the experiment. If I tried, something would definitely go wrong. Please, you have to believe me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon suddenly feels like renaming Fonta might not be enough...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: No problem! As long as you're willing to keep helping with the experiment, then putting your likenesses on the Fannta label would be more than fair!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So that means everyone who buys Fannta will get to see Paimon and {NICKNAME} on the label?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Yes! You'll be known around Teyvat. But for two scientific pioneers like yourselves, that's still a pretty modest reward. So, what do you say? Shall we keep going?

choices.text: Will Fann — Fonta's development team really agree to that?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: I've known Heinry for years. I'm sure he'll agree if I say the right words. If not... well, we can always add his name to the label too!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: After all, what we seek has never been glory, but scientific progress itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, let's get back to the experiment!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Excellent! I knew you were people of extraordinary insight. Once you're ready, I'll go set up the parameters for the next experiment.

choices.text: For the sake of scientific progress!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Are you ready? Shall we move on to the next experiment?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're ready!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Great, let's start the experiment!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Give us a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Alright, no problem. I could use some time to analyze the data you gathered earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Are you ready to begin the next experiment?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: F—Finally, it worked! Warriors, my name is Fanngel. I'm a researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I saw everything just now. You were absolutely incredible! May I ask your names?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers. Have you been stuck here for a long time?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: If not for the two of you, I might've been stuck much longer... You're the first ones to make it through the thunderstorm safely!

choices.text: Surely you should be the first one?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: N—No, of course not! I... don't have your luck.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: You probably won't believe me... but this abnormal weather is probably a result of my being cursed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cursed? Wait, do sciencey people really believe in that kind of thing?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Indeed. In fact, that's why I got into science in the first place — to find a way to break this curse. I know it sounds crazy, but if you'd gone through half the things I have, you'd understand.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Whenever I cook, even when I'm just mixing a salad, it somehow catches fire. If I hang out the laundry, a tornado is guaranteed to blow it away... Things like that happen to me every — single — day. I call it the "Fanngel Effect."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That really does sound unlucky... Isn't there a way to break the curse?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Science, of course! That's the only way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds reasonable enough, but something feels off...

choices.text: It sounds about as reasonable as Paimon single-handedly fighting Abyssal monsters...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmph, how about Paimon single-handedly fighting {NICKNAME}? Honestly... Paimon's always cheering the loudest when you're fighting!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: *sigh* I tried all the traditional methods when I was younger, but none of them worked. In the end, it was the Fontaine Research Institute that saved me. They taught me how to fight against it.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Since mixing salads caused fires, I invented a cooling system for food! In fact, that very system ended up being used in Fonta vending machines.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Now everyone can easily enjoy ice-cold Fonta, and that's thanks in part to the Fanngel Effect. Heinry's been so grateful to me for this, hehe.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Before coming here, I learned that the extreme weather in Nod-Krai could be incredibly dangerous, so I made sure to install a lightning protection device on the collector, just in case.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Without it, the experiment would have probably failed a dozen times by now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So science really did beat the curse!?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Uhm, you could say that... But, as you saw, I got pretty flustered just now because I overlooked one critical factor—

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: The collector might be fine, but with the Fanngel Effect following me around, there's no way I can conduct the experiment properly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you've just been running around like that ever since you got here... until we found you?

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: That's right. *sigh* The Institute saved me, so I couldn't bring myself to go back without something to show for it... That's why your arrival is such an unexpected turning point!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: As I mentioned earlier, I came here to study the safety of kuuvahki under extreme weather conditions. I believe it could be a much safer energy source than Arkhium!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: You've probably heard about the explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute, right? At its core, that accident happened because Arkhium is still too dangerous to use as an energy source.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course, we heard about it! You're looking at none other than an "Honorary Senior Researcher of the Fontaine Research Institute"!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Mr. Raimondo must think very highly of you. For most people, even earning the title of Assistant is quite an achievement.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Though I agree with Mr. Raimondo's views, things like Fonta don't really contribute much to science. What we truly need is a more reliable alternative to Arkhium.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: If my theory proves correct and kuuvahki really is a safer option... the Institute might even rename Fonta to "Fannta" in my honor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that really a possibility? That sounds amazing!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: So, may I ask for your help? If you're willing to help me complete my experiment and collect the data I need...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: I'll make sure to propose that both your names be added to Fannta!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Fann-{NICKNAME}-Paimon-ta? That's quite an impressive name!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's help!

choices.text: Alright, but I imagine sales will take quite a hit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You think the name's too long? Then let's go with "Fannta Paimon"!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're not joining the co-branding? How modest of you. I'll be sure to give you a special thanks in the acknowledgments section of my thesis!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: We managed to get the Airspace Data Collector into the air earlier, but unfortunately, it didn't quite get high enough. All you need to do now is lift it up a little more.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: To get it higher, you'll need to <color=#00E1FFFF>stack more assembly modules</color>. Simple and effective, huh? I'm counting on you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds simple enough. We've got this!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: In that case, shall we start setting things up? When adjusting the assembly modules, just make sure the <color=#00E1FFFF>blue strong "unipolar" field is facing the collector</color>.

choices.text: That sounds great.
Isn't a blessing usually the way to break a curse?
Then how did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Wonderful! With your help, I no longer have to worry about the Fanngel Effect messing up the experiment!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Hmm... Data sorting is a meticulous task. I'll have to remain fully focused...

choices.text: About your thesis...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Once my thesis is finished and published, I'll make sure to send you a copy. Well then, time for me to get back to my research...

choices.text: About kuuvahki...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Our understanding of kuuvahki is still quite limited. I'm considering spending more time in Nod-Krai to conduct further field research.

choices.text: About the collector's lightning protection...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: It's pretty effective, right? I take my research seriously, after all.

choices.text: Best of luck with your thesis!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: You too! Best of luck with your adventures!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: F—Finally, it worked! Warriors, my name is Fanngel. I'm a researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I saw everything just now. You were absolutely incredible! May I ask your names?

response.text: You've probably heard about the explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute, right? At its core, that accident happened because Arkhium is still too dangerous to use as an energy source.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: Though I agree with Mr. Raimondo's views, things like Fonta don't really contribute much to science. What we truly need is a more reliable alternative to Arkhium.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: If my theory proves correct and kuuvahki really is a safer option... the Institute might even rename Fonta to "Fannta" in my honor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that really a possibility? That sounds amazing!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: So, may I ask for your help? If you're willing to help me complete my experiment and collect the data I need...

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: I'll make sure to propose that both your names be added to Fannta!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Fann-{NICKNAME}-Paimon-ta? That's quite an impressive name!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's help!

choices.text: Alright, but I imagine sales will take quite a hit...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You think the name's too long? Then let's go with "Fannta Paimon"!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're not joining the co-branding? How modest of you. I'll be sure to give you a special thanks in the acknowledgments section of my thesis!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: We managed to get the Airspace Data Collector into the air earlier, but unfortunately, it didn't quite get high enough. All you need to do now is lift it up a little more.

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: To get it higher, you'll need to <color=#00E1FFFF>stack more assembly modules</color>. Simple and effective, huh? I'm counting on you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds simple enough. We've got this!

response.speaker: Fanngel
response.text: In that case, shall we start setting things up? When adjusting the assembly modules, just make sure the <color=#00E1FFFF>blue strong "unipolar" field is facing the collector</color>.

choices.text: That sounds great.
Isn't a blessing usually the way to break a curse?
Then how did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Give us a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Alright, no problem. I could use some time to analyze the data you gathered earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: This will be the final experiment. <color=#00E1FFFF>Channel the lightning to the lightning rod over there, then launch up and collect the data.</color> The lightning protection device in the Collector 2.0 will keep you safe.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I'll let you know as soon as we've got enough data. And I'll do everything I can to keep you safe. So, ready to go?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still need a little more time...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: That's fine — the more thorough the preparations, the smoother the experiment tends to go. Just come find me when you're ready!

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: The experiment parameters are all set. I'm counting on you to launch the collector.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Looks like the collector's beyond repair. That means these assembly modules are useless, too. *sigh* I've worked on this for so long...

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: The Fanngel Effect has definitely intensified... but this isn't the time to worry about that. I'll focus on checking the equipment first.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: Apart from the materials, could something else be going wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: See that lightning rod over there? I set it up specially for this experiment. It can convert kuuvahki into an upward force field.

dialogues.speaker: Fanngel
dialogues.text: I've already run the tests, and in theory it should work. Now it's up to you to put it into practice!
